# Isaac Lab: Four-legged robot Jacobian shape is normal but foot end blocks are almost all zeros; how to confirm and fix link index misalignment in the original thread?

> **Current answer:** Confirm that the index and data come from the same PhysX view. The original post used the rigid body view's find_bodies to retrieve root_physx_view.get_jacobians(), but at the time, the body view and articulation view's link ordering was different, so integer 4 did not correspond to the expected foot end. Maintainer merged commit e3c40acf, making Articulation.body_names follow PhysX articulation order and internally reordering body-view data. Old versions should use root_physx_view.shared_metatype.link_names for indexing; new versions should use the unified Articulation/root_physx_view interface.

## Key terms

- Jacobian matrix (雅可比矩阵)
- Rigid Body View (刚体视图)
- Articulation View (关节体视图)
- Link indexing (连杆索引)
- Finite difference (有限差分)

## Problem and symptoms

- How to check if the index used is from the same view when root_physx_view.get_jacobians() returns almost all zeros for the foot end?
- The questioner reads jacobian[0,4,0:3,-12:] as FL_foot, but the matrix is almost all zeros except one column.
- The same reading occurs in Go2 and ANYmal-C.

## Environment

- Isaac Lab/Orbit main; Isaac Sim 2023.1.1; Ubuntu 22.04; RTX 4090; CUDA 12.3; Unitree Go2 and ANYmal-C.

## Priority diagnostics

- Printed body_physx_view.prim_paths exported body names order and root_physx_view.shared_metatype.link_names to confirm index source and Jacobian source consistency.
- The ANYmal example shows body view ordered by each leg chain, while the articulation view lists four hip, then thigh, shank, and foot; same integer index corresponds to different links.

## Possible causes

- find_bodies uses rigid body view's body_names to return index, while Jacobian comes from PhysX articulation view; the two views had different link ordering at the time.

## Attempts

- The author reinterpreted the index based on the maintainer's provided articulation view link_names and confirmed that the original index was taking the wrong data.
- The maintainer merged commit e3c40acf, changing Articulation.body_names to follow PhysX articulation order and internally reordering articulation-link to body-view data.

## Effective fixes

- Old versions must use root_physx_view.shared_metatype.link_names to index data.
- Upgrade to Orbit 0.14.0 or later Isaac Lab versions, using the unified Articulation.body_names/root_physx_view interface, and no longer mixing the deprecated body_physx_view.

## Result

- The author confirmed the index messed things up; the maintainer released the fix and stated it covers Jacobian, inertia matrix, etc., link data consistency, and Issue completed is closed.

## Limitations

- The fix addresses link ordering consistency, and does not imply any Jacobian value anomaly is caused by index mismatch.
- Different Isaac Lab versions have changed public property names, so diagnosis should use the Articulation API for the current version.

## Safety notes

- Before real-world WBC, each Jacobian row block should be automatically asserted against the link name, and direction checked with finite difference or known joint motion to avoid issuing control commands to the wrong link.
